notes: Account overview: CompileWave builds an IDE-embedded copilot (VS Code + JetBrains) focused on low-latency streaming completions and in-editor multi-line suggestions.
Primary ask: TTFT and streaming jitter guarantees for IDE UX; token-budget controls to avoid runaway completions while keeping suggestions fluid.
TTFT targets (customer): median <= 90ms, p95 <= 180ms for first token when model is hot (dedicated pool). Jitter budget: < 30ms typical between subsequent token arrivals.
Throughput: ~1k concurrent users per cluster during peak internal beta; typical concurrency for pilot: 100-200. Average token length per completion: 8-80 tokens depending on snippet length.
Token budget strategy requested: client-driven dynamic budgets (based on file complexity + cursor context), server-enforced hard cap, and soft warnings via token-cost headers.

Backpressure behaviour: prefer graceful degradation (send partial completion + clear 'more-available' flag) over blocking editor thread. Want clean client cancellation semantics and KV-cache reuse across small repeated completions.
Model/version pinning: need stable pin for GA (7B quantized for quick responses) with easy rollback to 13B for quality-sensitive routes; want rollout A/B and canary support.

Routing: prefer dedicated pool in us-west1 for primary users, fallback to hosted smaller model in us-east when capacity constrained. Must support deterministic fallback that preserves completion format.
Security: SSO/SAML, per-route audit logs, KMS integration for keys. Also asked about retention controls and EU residency for EU-based engineering teams.
Quote from CTO (call 2026-02-25): 'If first token isn't visible within a keyboard frame, devs drop the suggestion — TTFT is everything.'

Technical constraints: existing editor extension uses streaming SSE; requires small-chunk streaming (prefer 32-64 token chunks) and immediate first token emit. Existing infra assumes token-level streaming; developer SDK changes have cost implications.

Perf/benchmarks: attached internal bench shows warm median TTFT 78ms on their local sim when using 7B quantized; cold starts spike ~800ms. Want Redwood to replicate warm behaviour on Dedicated and show p95 under load.
Commercial: interest in Dedicated with committed nodes for predictable latency; Optimize for token-budget tuning recommendations to reduce unit cost while maintaining quality.
Procurement: legal sent custom DPA on 2026-02-28; procurement kick-off planned after POC. Forecasted ARR if successful: $60k-$120k ARR.
Risks: UI changes required if streaming jitter > 40ms; internal timeline aggressive — GA in Q3 2026.
